title: Phuket 3 Days 2 Nights 2026 — Old Town, Beaches & Island Tour | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: An unhurried 3-day, 2-night Phuket plan: Old Town and local food, a full day on a Phi Phi or Phang Nga Bay island tour, beaches and a Promthep Cape sunset — with real timings, prices, and routes.
keywords: Phuket 3 days 2 nights, Phuket itinerary, Phi Phi island tour, Phang Nga Bay, Phuket Old Town, Promthep Cape
ogTitle: Phuket in 3 Days, 2 Nights — Old Town, Island Tour & Beaches
ogDesc: A doable 3-day, 2-night Phuket itinerary: Old Town day, island-tour day, beach day — with real timings, prices, restaurants, and the best sunset spot.
intro: Three days and two nights is about the perfect length for Phuket — not as rushed as a single day, but not so long you're scrambling to fill the time. We've put day one in the Sino-Portuguese Old Town, eating dim sum and wandering past century-old shophouses with your camera out. Day two is a full day at sea on a Phi Phi or Phang Nga Bay island tour (your pick). Then the last day eases off, picking up the pretty west-coast beaches and closing with sunset at Promthep Cape. Every stretch comes with timings, realistic ballpark prices, and a route you can just follow.
chips: ⛵ Phi Phi / Phang Nga Bay tour

blocks.html: Phuket is bigger than most people expect — driving from the Old Town out to Promthep Cape takes nearly an hour. Plan the trip haphazardly and you'll spend more time in the car than actually seeing anything. So this 3-day, 2-night plan splits into three clear themes — city day, sea day, beach day — to save you from criss-crossing the island. Day two is the island tour, which you'll need to book ahead for and start early; the other two days are relaxed walking days.

blocks.title: Book the island tour ahead + pick the right zone to stay
blocks.html: On day two the pickup at your hotel is very early (around 07:00–08:00). Booking online a day or two ahead gets you a better price and guarantees your seat. For where to stay, we'd book both nights in the same zone so you're not lugging bags around. If you're into cafés and food, stay in the Old Town; if you're more about swimming and nightlife, stay in Patong. Either zone, the island tours will come and pick you up.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Sino-Portuguese Old Town, eating your way through

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Morning dim sum · old shophouses · a Michelin southern lunch

items.activity: Breakfast dim sum at Boonrat Dim Sum
items.note: One of Phuket town's old-school dim sum spots, made to a traditional Cantonese recipe. It opens very early — only around 6–10 am — and fills up fast, so earlier is better. Plates are a few tens of baht each; you'll be full for under ฿150/person.

items.activity: Wander the Old Town — Thalang Road, Soi Romanee, Sino-Portuguese shophouses
items.note: Pastel shophouses over a hundred years old. Thalang Road and Soi Romanee are the favourite photo corners, and there's local-food-themed street art dotted around to hunt down. An easy stroll of about 1.5 hours, no entry fee, and the morning sun is still gentle.

items.activity: Café break in the Old Town — Kor Ra Kang or a Thalang Road café
items.note: Kor Ra Kang is a café with pink flowers covering the walls — very photogenic, drinks around ฿90–160. The area is full of cafés roasting their own beans, with plenty within easy walking distance to pick from.

items.activity: Southern/Phuket lunch at Tu Kab Khao
items.note: Set in an old building on Phang Nga Road, serving southern Thai and local Phuket dishes; it's a Michelin-listed spot. Open 11:00–24:00, lunch runs around ฿300–500/person. It gets busy at midday, so booking ahead is a good idea.

items.activity: Try the legendary Hokkien mee at Mee Ton Poe
items.note: Phuket-style stir-fried Hokkien mee with soft yellow noodles, near the Clock Tower roundabout. Open until early evening, a few tens of baht a plate. If you're still full from lunch, save it for a light afternoon bite.

items.activity: Back to the hotel to check in, then out for a second round of street art and old shophouses
items.note: By late afternoon the sun softens — good for relaxed photos of Soi Romanee, Dibuk Road, and Phang Nga Road before the shops light up in the evening.

items.activity: Dinner — Raya Restaurant (southern food in an old wooden house) or seafood in town
items.note: Raya sits in an old wooden house on Dibuk Road, serving proper southern Thai and Phuket cooking. Open 10:00–22:00, around ฿350–600/person. If you happen to be here on a Sunday, swap it for the Lard Yai Walking Street on Thalang Road (open around 16:00–22:00) and eat your way through the market instead.

blocks.title: Turn in early tonight
blocks.html: Tomorrow is the island-tour day with a very early pickup. Pack your swimwear, sunscreen (go for the reef-safe kind), a towel, and a waterproof phone pouch tonight, so you're not scrambling in the morning.

blocks.text: Day 2 — A full day at sea, picking the right island tour

blocks.html: Today is the highlight of the trip. You've got two main routes to choose between — the Phi Phi Islands + Maya Bay if you want clear water, snorkelling over coral, and postcard-perfect beach photos; or Phang Nga Bay + James Bond Island if you're more into nature, paddling a canoe through sea caves, and limestone-karst views rising out of the water. Pick one — both eat up a full day.

items.activity: Tour van picks you up at the hotel
items.note: Pickup time depends on your zone — the Old Town and Patong are usually collected around 07:00–08:00. Carry your ID or passport, and have a light breakfast at the hotel first.

items.activity: Arrive at the pier, listen to the briefing, then board the speedboat
items.note: Most tours leave from a pier on the east side (such as Rassada Pier). The speedboat to Phi Phi takes about an hour, and the swell can pick up in stretches — if you get seasick, take something before you board.

items.activity: Route A — Phi Phi: Maya Bay, Pileh Lagoon, snorkelling
items.note: Maya Bay, made famous by The Beach, is open to visitors 1 Oct–31 Jul and closed for recovery 1 Aug–30 Sep every year. Stop to snorkel over the coral, see the emerald water of Pileh Lagoon and Monkey Bay. The full-day tour includes a buffet lunch, around ฿1,300–1,800/person (national park fees are extra, collected on the spot).

items.activity: Route B — Phang Nga Bay: James Bond Island, canoeing through caves
items.note: The option for nature lovers: cruise past Khao Tapu (James Bond Island) and paddle a canoe through the sea caves and mangroves at Koh Hong, with a guide doing the paddling. Around ฿1,500–2,500/person depending on the boat type (a big boat is cheaper, a speedboat is faster). Lunch included.

items.activity: Lunch on an island / on the boat
items.note: The full-day tour includes a buffet or set lunch, drinking water, tea and coffee, and fruit. Most often it's eaten at Khai Island (Route A) or the tour's rest stop (Route B).

items.activity: Stop at Khai Island / a final snorkel spot, swim off the beach
items.note: On the way back there's usually a stop at Khai Island — clear water, lots of fish, with umbrellas and loungers to rent. Watch out for the extra island charges that are billed separately; always ask the price before you use anything.

items.activity: Boat heads back to shore
items.note: The speedboat back takes about an hour. The afternoon sun can be strong, so reapply sunscreen and throw on a long-sleeve top to avoid burning.

items.activity: Dropped back at the hotel, rest, then find dinner nearby
items.note: You'll be tired from the sun and seawater, so keep dinner easy and close to the hotel. If you're staying in Patong, you can walk around Bangla Road or Jungceylon for food.

blocks.title: Maya Bay closes seasonally
blocks.html: If you come 1 Aug–30 Sep, Maya Bay is closed for recovery every year. The Phi Phi tour still runs, but you won't be able to land at Maya Bay — check with the tour operator before booking, or pick Route B to Phang Nga Bay instead, which runs all year round.

blocks.text: Day 3 — West-coast beaches, closing with the sunset

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: West-coast beaches · the three-bay viewpoint · Promthep Cape

items.activity: Breakfast — kopi + Phuket khanom jeen, or old-school coffee
items.note: Phuket has a kopi (old-school coffee) culture, paired with dim sum or southern-style khanom jeen in crab curry sauce. An easy breakfast, around ฿80–150/person, before you check out and leave your bags at the hotel.

items.activity: Swim at Kata or Karon Beach (west coast)
items.note: Kata and Karon have fine white sand and gentler surf than Patong — good for a morning swim before the crowds arrive. Loungers and umbrellas rent for around ฿200–300. In the rainy season (May–Oct), if you see a red flag, do not go in the water under any circumstances.

items.activity: Seafood lunch around Kata / Rawai
items.note: Seafood places charge by weight — pick one with clearly posted prices that locals actually go to, around ฿300–600/person. Rawai Beach has fish stalls where you can choose your own fresh catch.

items.activity: Karon Viewpoint (the three-bay viewpoint)
items.note: A roadside pull-off on the way south, taking in Kata Noi, Kata, and Karon all in one frame. No entry fee, and the afternoon light is lovely. A quick photo stop and you're back on the road.

items.activity: Stop at Wat Chalong (if you have time) to pay respects before Promthep Cape
items.note: Phuket's most famous temple, home to Luang Pho Cham, with handsome architecture. Open around 07:00–17:00, no entry fee, dress modestly. About 40 minutes here is plenty.

items.activity: Arrive at Promthep Cape and claim a spot for the sunset
items.note: The sunset spot most people rate as the island's best, facing out over the Andaman Sea to the west. Open 24 hours, no entry fee. Arrive before 5 pm to get a good spot — on weekends it's very busy and the car park fills fast.

items.activity: Sunset, then on to Phuket Airport (HKT)
items.note: Sunset is around 6:30 pm in the middle of the year. From Promthep Cape to the airport is about an hour, which works out perfectly if you're on an evening flight. If you fly earlier, skip Promthep Cape and head straight to the airport, leaving at least 2.5–3 hours for check-in.

blocks.text: How to pick your day-2 island tour to match your style

items.name: Phi Phi Islands + Maya Bay
items.blurb: The clearest water — swimming, snorkelling, postcard-level beach photos. Great if you love a stunning sea, but it's crowded and Maya Bay closes Aug–Sep.

items.name: Phang Nga Bay + James Bond Island
items.blurb: Limestone karsts rising out of the sea, canoeing through caves and mangroves, a quieter atmosphere. Runs all year — good for nature lovers and families.

items.name: Khai Island half-day
items.blurb: The option if you're short on time or travelling with small kids — clear water, plenty of fish, a short boat ride, leaving your afternoon free for other things.

blocks.text: Phuket food you shouldn't miss on the trip

items.name: Morning dim sum (Boonrat Dim Sum)
items.blurb: Traditional Cantonese-recipe dim sum — har gow, siu mai, steamed buns, hot off the steamer. A classic Phuket breakfast that opens very early and sells out fast.

items.name: Hokkien mee (Mee Ton Poe)
items.blurb: Phuket-style stir-fried yellow noodles in a little gravy, with pork, prawns, and squid — a local dish that's hard to find elsewhere.
items.meta: Lunch–afternoon · near the Clock Tower roundabout

items.name: Michelin southern food (Tu Kab Khao / Raya)
items.blurb: Bold southern Thai and local Phuket cooking — moo hong, stir-fried sator, crab curry with cha-plu leaves — in atmospheric old buildings and houses.

items.name: Phuket khanom jeen in crab curry sauce
items.blurb: Rice noodles under a rich southern-style crab curry, eaten with fresh vegetables and a boiled egg — a popular breakfast alongside kopi.

items.name: O-aew
items.blurb: Phuket's signature cold dessert — a jelly made from banana seeds, topped with red syrup and shaved ice. A great cooler after a walk around town.

items.name: Rawai / Kata seafood
items.blurb: Pick your fresh catch from the fish stalls, have it weighed, then order it cooked — lobster, blue crab, shellfish, steamed grouper in soy. Fresh and good value if you choose the right place.

items.name: Roti & cha chak
items.blurb: Roti that's crisp outside and soft inside, drizzled with condensed milk, alongside hot pulled tea — an afternoon-to-evening snack you'll find all over town.

items.name: Tao so (to take home)
items.blurb: Thin-pastry pastries with mung-bean or taro filling — a Phuket souvenir classic you can buy to take back. Go for the shops locals queue at.

blocks.text: Rough budget per person (3 days, 2 nights)

items: 2 nights' accommodation — a mid-range hotel in the Old Town/Patong at ฿900–2,000/night (split between 2 people), so roughly ฿900–2,000/person
Day-2 island tour — Phi Phi around ฿1,300–1,800 / Phang Nga Bay around ฿1,500–2,500, not counting national park fees collected on the spot
Food — 7–8 meals, around ฿1,200–2,200 for the whole trip, depending on whether you go for seafood or street food
Getting around the island — car rental ฿900–1,400/day, or a motorbike ฿250–350/day plus fuel (you won't need a vehicle on tour day, since pickup and drop-off are included)
Attraction entry — the Old Town, the viewpoints, Promthep Cape, and Wat Chalong are all free; only the marine national park fees on tour day apply

blocks.text: Tips to make the trip run smoother

items: Check the season before booking — May–Oct is the rainy season, when the west-coast surf gets rough in stretches and some island tours may be cancelled if the swell is high. Nov–Apr brings clear water and good sun, but more crowds and pricier rooms.

Put the tour day in the middle of the trip — that gives you a buffer if your first-day flight is delayed, and saves the last day for things close to your hotel. If heavy rain cancels the tour day, you can still shift it to another day.
Pack for sun and water — reef-safe sunscreen, a hat, sunglasses, a long-sleeve top, and a waterproof phone pouch. The sun off the sea in Phuket is stronger than you'd think.
Watch out for jet skis / beachfront tours — always agree on the price and photograph the condition of the equipment before you use it, to avoid being charged for 'damage' later.
Morning dim sum sells out fast — several of the old-school places close before noon, so plan breakfast before 9 am to be safe.

Leave time between Promthep Cape and the airport — if you want to catch the sunset on your last day and then fly out, choose a later flight, since it's about an hour from Promthep Cape to the airport.

faq.q: Is 3 days, 2 nights enough for Phuket?
faq.a: Yes, and it's about the right length. Split it into an Old Town day, a full island-tour day, and a day picking up the west-coast beaches and closing with the sunset, and you'll cover the Sino-Portuguese culture, the outer islands, and the local food without running yourself ragged all day.

faq.q: For day 2, should I pick the Phi Phi or the Phang Nga Bay tour?
faq.a: If you want clear water, snorkelling, and pretty beach photos, go for Phi Phi + Maya Bay (but note Maya Bay closes 1 Aug–30 Sep every year). If you prefer nature, paddling through sea caves, limestone-karst views, and a quieter atmosphere, choose Phang Nga Bay + James Bond Island, which runs all year round.

faq.q: Roughly how much is an island tour, and what's included?
faq.a: A full-day Phi Phi tour runs around ฿1,300–1,800/person, and Phang Nga Bay around ฿1,500–2,500/person. Most include hotel pickup and drop-off, lunch, snorkelling gear, tea and coffee, and fruit — but the marine national park fee is usually collected separately on the spot, so ask the operator to be clear before you book.

faq.q: Which zone should I stay in for this 3-day plan?
faq.a: We'd stay in one zone for both nights so you don't have to move your bags. If you like cafés and food, stay in the Old Town for an easy first day of sightseeing. If you're more about swimming and a lively night scene, stay in Patong. Either zone gets island-tour pickup and can drive to the west-coast beaches and Promthep Cape on the last day.

faq.q: Can I do this plan without driving myself?
faq.a: Yes. On day 2 the island tour already includes hotel pickup and drop-off, so no vehicle needed, and the Old Town day is all on foot. For the last day, which runs between several stops (beaches, viewpoint, Promthep Cape, airport), we'd suggest hiring a car with a driver for the afternoon-to-evening, starting around ฿1,500–2,000, or calling a Grab leg by leg.
